lines.t: Yeah… South side…
Double cup of that livin’ water, feel me?
We don’t bow to self no more…
I was my own god, dancin’ in the flame,
Mirror in the temple, worshipin’ my name,
Heart full of pride, mind full of game,
Then YahuShua came, everything got changed.I was my own god, king of my pain,
Numbin’ all the trauma, drownin’ in the shame,
Now I lay it down, nail it to the frame,
All hail The Most High, He the only one to reign.
South side steppin’, but my soul was in a drought,
Whole life chasin’ clout, but my spirit tappin’ out,
Actin’ like a boss, really just a slave to doubt,
Put a crown on my flesh, that’s a dead man’s route.Pain in my chest, so I built my own throne,
Turned hurt into hustle, made sin my home,
Past wounds talk loud when you feel alone,
So I bowed to my scars, like they carved in stone.Idol in the mirror, that’s a demon in disguise,
Satan in the garden still sellin’ me lies,
“Be your own god, boy, open up your eyes,”
But every step of pride is a step to my demise.All gas, no brakes on that self‑made trip,
Heart cold, dark soul, with a diamond‑cut drip,
But the ice in my chain couldn’t heal that rip,
Only blood on the cross got a real tight grip.
I was my own god, dancin’ in the flame,
Mirror in the temple, worshipin’ my name,
Heart full of pride, mind full of game,
Then YahuShua came, everything got changed.I was my own god, king of my pain,
Numbin’ all the trauma, drownin’ in the shame,
Now I lay it down, nail it to the frame,
All hail The Most High, He the only one to reign.
Whole world trained us to worship that self,
Stackin’ up sin like it’s spiritual wealth,
Pain in the stash, pride on the shelf,
Die for the drip, but we starvin’ for help.Scrolls in my phone, doctrine in my head,
But I never let it cut where the ego bled,
I could quote every verse like I’m well‑read,
Still livin’ like a pharaoh with a heart of lead.He said, “Let go,” but I loved my chains,
Loved bein’ the victim, loved my stains,
Loved playin’ god in my private lanes,
Til grace hit hard like a train through my veins.He exposed that idol, put my soul on blast,
Showed me every fake crown that I tried to cast,
Every time I chose self, every time I chose cash,
Every secret little throne that I built to last.Then He said, “Lay down that counterfeit king,
I’ma crush that image, let My freedom ring,
You want more of Me? Then surrender that thing,
You can’t serve two masters, choose who you bring.”

Mirror in the temple, worshipin’ my name,
Heart full of pride, mind full of game,
Then YahuShua came, everything got changed.I was my own god, king of my pain,
Numbin’ all the trauma, drownin’ in the shame,
Now I lay it down, nail it to the frame,
All hail The Most High, He the only one to reign.
Now when that self rise up in my house, I check it,
“Sit down, flesh, YahuShua run the records,”
I don’t need to be right, I just need to stay submitted,
Better to be broken than fake and never admit it.Misunderstood by my own? Yeah, that cut real deep,
But I’d rather lose an argument than grieve His sheep,
Rather bite my tongue than sow what I can’t reap,
I’m layin’ down my crown every day that I breathe.Self‑god dead, but he try to resurrect,
In the heat of a fight or a lack of respect,
That’s when I step back, put my pride in check,
“Only One on the throne,” that’s the heart project.South side swingin’ but my spirit in His hand,
No more bowin’ to my wound, I’ma bow to The Lamb,
Used to flex for the ‘Gram, now I die to the ‘Gram,
‘Cause eternity laughin’ at a temporary brand.I ain’t chasin’ my image, I’m chasin’ His face,
Ain’t buildin’ my kingdom, I’m livin’ by grace,
He exposed my self‑worship, called it out as disgrace,
Then He flooded my confession with a holy embrace.
I was my own god, dancin’ in the flame,
Mirror in the temple, worshipin’ my name,
Heart full of pride, mind full of game,
Then YahuShua came, everything got changed.I was my own god, king of my pain,
Numbin’ all the trauma, drownin’ in the shame,
Now I lay it down, nail it to the frame,
All hail The Most High, He the only one to reign.
Yeah…
Self off the throne, King on the seat,
From the south side blocks to the glass‑clear streets,
We kill that idol every time we hit our knees,
More of Him, less of me – that’s the only way to breathe.
